points.description: Names the property: there is a single unique path between every pair of nodes in the tree (equivalently, the tree is loop-free and connects all nodes), so packets are not duplicated unnecessarily. Equivalent wording such as 'no loops, yet all nodes are included' earns the mark.
Explains that multicast group membership information is added to the link state packets, since each router knows its own groups but not which other routers belong to them.

Explains that once the full topology and group information have been flooded to all nodes, each node builds the multicast spanning tree locally from its complete state information, using an algorithm such as Prim's or Kruskal's. Any correct equivalent tree-construction method earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (1) require the unique-path/loop-free property, the addition of group membership to link state packets, and local tree construction from the full topology (Prim or Kruskal). Marks are awarded per point, and a point is missed entirely if its idea is absent. The answer should be read as a whole, so an answer that gives the link state modification without mentioning that every node has the full topology should lose P3.
